### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s).

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5afb74a433a132294b6d566a97882daf637d9c85` — the merge of head `e7821fc953df6b2c45d87c0239cdd40c54a0487b` into base `2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5afb74a433a132294b6d566a97882daf637d9c85 && git checkout 5afb74a433a132294b6d566a97882daf637d9c85
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950 e7821fc953df6b2c45d87c0239cdd40c54a0487b && git checkout -B drift-repro 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950 && git merge --no-ff e7821fc953df6b2c45d87c0239cdd40c54a0487b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2513e3ad90dbba61b05230693a713465c7828950` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

I read `hookBindingGroups` and the teardown in `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` at this head, `ownPackageFunction` in `packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts` on `origin/main`, the PR body (FROM → TO, census, tests) and card #32349. Nothing was built or run.

### Red lines 1 and 2: agree

- **Rows 1–5 (widenings)** apply ADR-0150 D3 step 1 (same package first): a body's flow and hook reach that body's own function. Nothing reaches a holder outside D3's order.
- **Row 6 (narrowing)** matches the hook binder's own-package rule on `main` (`ownPackageFunction`, #32073: "own package only — a holder in the hook's closure … is not this package's code"). Separately installed packages already answer this way; the composed artifact was the exception. Fail-closed, logged at `error`.
- **Row 7** is D3 exactly: in the closure ⇒ resolved, else `outside-closure` with candidates.
- **Rows 10 and 13** pick nothing: an undeclared function two owners' hooks name stays with the artifact's owner, and a residual twin binds neither copy with `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming the body (#32355's job shape). Ambiguity reported, never guessed.
- **Row 8 / teardown:** every recorded and newly named owner is unbound; a dropped body's functions leave the engine. No stale holder is left to answer a bare read.

### Red line 3: owed

**E1, must-fix: two moved answers are not in the FROM → TO table.** A function declared by exactly ONE body is registered under that body (`declaring.length === 1 ⇒ [ownerOf(declaring[0])]`). Its hook can still be grouped under the artifact's owner, and the owner's bind then cannot reach it through `ownPackageFunction`. By reading:

- **E1-a.** A residual hook (no body declares the hook; the top level carries it) whose `handler` names a function only body B (B ≠ the artifact's own) declares. FROM: bound under `app:A`, running B's function. TO: the hook is grouped under `app:A` and the function under `app:B`, so the bind refuses it with `INVALID_REFERENCE`.
- **E1-b.** A hook name two or more bodies carry that `namespaceNameConflicts` does NOT hold apart (the hooks stay under the artifact's owner), where one of those hooks names a function only body B (B ≠ the artifact's own) declares. Same FROM → TO. If `composeStacks` or the install gate refuses such a pair before the binder runs, say so with the line that refuses it, and this half is unreachable.

Both are fail-closed, so no guess is made, but each is an undeclared narrowing: the epic body requires every child PR to declare each moved answer with its Clause-② arm. Do one of two things for each: add the row (FROM / TO / evidence) to the table, the Clause-② prose and the changeset, with a pin; or keep `main`'s outcome by placing the hook with its function, and pin that. Either answer passes the red lines. First-party reach stays 0 (the census holds: no shipped multi-package artifact declares a hook).

### Non-blocking notes

- **N1.** Row 6's fix sentence ("put the function in B's body or move the hook to A") is right. E1-a's would be "declare the function at the top level or move the hook into B".
- **N2.** The ordering note (owners' hooks may fire grouped by body at one priority) is declared in Acceptance notes; it should also be a line in the changeset, since an author can observe it.

### Order

This PR touches only `packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`, its test and changeset. It shares no file with #32214 or #32327, so it is outside the epic's serial order. BREAKING ⇒ the maintainer's word before queueing, as the lane says.

Check-runs read twice: 22:36Z (one `Check Changeset` run still in progress) and 22:41:56Z (all completed: every run `success` or `skipped`, none failed, none pending; `mergeable_state: clean`). The skipped ones are the opt-in and UI jobs.

**Outcome: FAIL on one must-fix (M1).** The code does what the card asks and I could not break the binder on the declared shapes. What fails is the declaration: two answers move for a manifest-less input (the ADR-0130 residual) that neither the 14-row table, the `Clause-②:` line nor the changeset lists, and one changeset sentence is false against the tree. The remedy is text plus one pin, or a rule change if the epic seat prefers one.

### ① Derived judgments

Each row of the PR body's FROM → TO table, judged against the head's `hookBindingGroups` / `bindAppArtifactHandlers` and the cited code on `main`:

| # | Verdict | Basis in the tree |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | right | a name one body's `functions` declares goes to that body's group (`declaredBy`, one declarer) |
| 2 | right | one holder of the hook name ⇒ `groupOf(ownerOf(body))`; exceptions are rows 10 and 13 |
| 3 | right | `resolvePackageScopedFunction` takes the caller's own holder first; base had only `[A]`, refused `outside-closure` |
| 4 | right | `ownPackageFunction` reads `functionHoldersOf(name).packageItem(B)` with the bind's `packageId`, now `app:B` |
| 5 | right | `heldApart` asks `namespaceNameConflicts` per holder; each body's own hooks bind once (`split`) |
| 6 | right, narrowing | B's group holds no function of the name, the binder refuses `INVALID_REFERENCE`, logs at error, continues (non-strict) |
| 7 | right, narrowing | follows from row 1 and the resolver's step 2/3; no permanent pin (S3) |
| 8 | right | teardown removes hooks and actions of `owner ∪ previous ∪ bound`, and functions of `previous` not in `owner ∪ bound` |
| 9 | right for a body-declared function; **wrong** in "A's own and the residual's" | see M1 (a): a top-level function one other body's hook names leaves `app:A` |
| 10 | right | the shared rule moves every hook naming the undeclared function to the artifact's owner; one package holder |
| 11 | right as worded | holds only while a hook under the artifact's owner names the function; see M1 (a) |
| 12 | right | `artifactBodies` answers `undefined`, one group under `owner`, same collectors, same single `bindHooks` |
| 13 | right, narrowing | `toBodies && residualCarries` refuses the name; one error with `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `ambiguous-in-environment`, `packages` |
| 14 | right | the one holder is the artifact's own body, `toBodies` is false, both copies go under `owner` |

Is the narrowing set exactly rows 6, 7, 13 and the engine calls of row 9? **No.** Probed shapes:

- **Extensions-only body, the artifact's own body, a single-body `packages[]`, a bundle with `packages: []`:** unchanged or as the table says. No finding.
- **A top-level function named by one body's hook: moved, unlisted.** M1 (a).
- **A residual hook naming a function only a non-own body declares: refused, unlisted.** M1 (b).
- **Hook firing order across bodies: moved, in the acceptance notes only.** S2.
- **A function two bodies declare** (off `composeStacks`, which refuses the pair with `STACK_COMPOSE_FUNCTION_CONFLICT`; a hand-written artifact only): registered under the artifact's owner, so the non-own body's hook naming it is refused where base bound it. Stated in "What changes", not in the table. Nit N1.

**M1 (must-fix) — two moved answers for the residual are undeclared, and one changeset sentence is false.**

(a) A function no body declares that the hooks of exactly one body B (not the artifact's own) name, and no hook under the artifact's owner names. In `hookBindingGroups` its owners are `namedBy.get(name)`, which is `{app:B}`, so it is registered under `app:B` alone. Base registered every function under `app:A`. For the ref `os build` lowers out of B's hook this is the intended answer (the CONTROL pin's first half, itself a moved answer the table does not carry). For a function a manifest-less input declares, it moves these answers:
- `functionHoldersOf(F).packageItem(A)`: FROM the entry TO `undefined`; `packageItem(B)`: FROM `undefined` TO the entry.
- `unregisterFunctionsByPackage('app:A')`: FROM removing it TO leaving it.
- **Narrowing:** a flow of the artifact's own package (body A's, or the residual's, which registers under the artifact's id) whose `script` node names F: FROM resolved as its own TO B's through A's declared closure, else refused `outside-closure`.
- Widening: a body-B flow naming F resolves it as its own.

This contradicts row 9 and the changeset's "TO removing the artifact's own package's (and the top level's)". It also sits badly beside the PR's own reason for row 13 ("the residual's function not attributed to B"): here the residual's function is attributed to B because B's hook names it, while the same reference to a function body A declares is refused (row 6).

(b) A residual hook whose `handler` names a function only a non-own body B declares: the hook stays under `app:A`, the function goes to `app:B`, and the binder refuses the hook `INVALID_REFERENCE`. Base bound it. The `Clause-②:` line and the BREAKING paragraph speak only of "a hook in one package body".

First-party count for both is 0 by the PR's own census (the one multi-package example declares no hook, function or flow), so the level in ② stands. To clear M1: add the two rows to the table, the `Clause-②:` line and the changeset (correcting "(and the top level's)"), with a pin for (a)'s holder; or change the rule and declare that instead. See ③ for the design question this raises.

### ② Semver level

Holds. The diff publishes from `@objectstack/runtime` alone; the changeset is `'@objectstack/runtime': minor` and carries both line-initial declarations, the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO fixes and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head. `Metadata-protocol: semantic` takes at least `minor`, which is what ships.

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right against the tree and correctly replaces the claim's `no`: rows 6, 7 and 13 narrow, and the line also states the widening. It is incomplete by M1.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is defensible (the function a `handler` or `script` name reaches changes) and is the claim's value. Nit N2: the siblings #32073, #32355 and #32071 declared `none` / `patch` for the same kind of move. Over-declaring is the safe side; the seat may want one convention.

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report (comment 6808696356) carries `open_questions: []`, five `deviations` and one `out_of_scope_findings` entry.

- **Deviation 1, `Clause-②` corrected to `yes (narrowing)`:** answered. Correct, see ②.
- **Deviation 2, PR body stale for the head:** answered. The body I read describes `162d67a0`: row 13, pin (g) and the corrected acceptance note are in it.
- **Deviation 3, no assignee on `pr_create`:** escalated to the seat. It is a conflict between the dispatch order and `os-dev.md`, not a contract matter, and I did not read the dispatch order.
- **Deviation 4, repo-wide `pnpm lint` not run locally:** answered by the head's `Lint · ESLint` and `Lint & Repo Gates`, both `success`.
- **Deviation 5, first cloud-connection run failed on an unbuilt dist:** answered by `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, all `success`.
- **Out of scope, #32333's pending changeset:** escalated to the seat. `.changeset/32245-compose-object-less-action-per-namespace.md` on `main` still ends "Hooks and functions stay under the artifact's owner.", which this PR makes false in the same release notes. It needs a card or an edit by its owner.
- **Report line "PR check-runs: not yet read":** answered above.
- **Card: "Epic red-line review before landing":** still owed; not this record's to give.
- **Escalated to the epic seat (design, with M1):** a top-level function is indistinguishable in the artifact from a ref `os build` lowered out of a body's hook, so the binder gives it to the one body whose hook names it. Is that the ruled answer for a function the residual declares, or should such a reference be refused as row 6 refuses a body's? Either is declarable; the PR picks one without saying so.
- File surface: inside the claim. Three files; no fenced path touched; `hook-binder.ts` unchanged as stated. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, body signed by the seat.

### ④ Design judgment

Against ADR-0150 D3 (own package, then declared closure, then a refusal) and D4 (the function registry row: resolved in the package of its referrer), the change holds: a body's hooks and functions now sit under the package the two by-package readers ask for, and no bare name is resolved to a package on a guess. What I tried to break:

- **Teardown on re-bind:** holds. Every recorded owner and every newly named owner loses its hooks and actions; a dropped body's functions leave both the bare map and the holder set; an owner still named keeps its functions, replaced by name. The record is a superset (written before the withheld filter and any bind failure).
- **Per-group try/catch:** holds. The binder is non-strict, so one hook's refusal never throws; a whole group fails only on a thrown bind (a post-seal function-claim conflict, a runner fault). That owner is left torn down, the others bound, with one error naming the owner. This matches the module's stated failure posture.
- **Residual-twin count:** holds on both emitted shapes. A body carrying two hooks of one name counts two against two copies (additive) or two against itself (option B); a residual copy makes it three against two.
- **A function two bodies declare:** under the artifact's owner, one holder. N1.
- **Shared undeclared function:** holds; one package holder, nothing for the seal to report.
- **`boundOwnersByEngine` across engines:** holds. A `WeakMap` per engine object, keyed by the artifact's owner, so two engines and two artifacts never share a record.

Findings:

- **M1, must-fix:** in ①.
- **S1, should-fix:** a function whose owner changes between two binds of one artifact, while the old owner is still named, keeps its old registration. Example: an undeclared function named by B's hook in the first bind and by A's and B's in the second moves to `app:A`, and the stale entry stays under `app:B`. Two package holders then exist, B's hooks and flows can still reach the stale one, and after the cold-boot seal `claimBareNameFunctions` throws for the gaining owner, which leaves that whole group unbound. Base could not reach this: every function had one owner. Likewise a dropped body's function claim stays in the registry (`unregisterFunctionsByPackage` is the engine's; claims are released only by `uninstallPackage`). Reachable only where a bundle with callables is re-bound on a live engine (the exported binder called twice; not the JSON install-local door), so not blocking. Unregister a still-named owner's functions that the new bind no longer gives it.
- **S2, should-fix:** hook firing order within one priority moves (the engine's sort is stable, so ties follow registration order): owners now bind group by group, and hooks the shared rule moves are appended to the artifact owner's group. The PR says so in its acceptance notes only. It belongs in the table and the changeset.
- **S3, should-fix:** row 7 is a declared BREAKING arm with no permanent pin ("probe, not pinned").
- **N1, nit:** the two-bodies-declare-one-function consequence (first list in ①) is not in the table.
- **N2, nit:** in ②.
- **N3, nit:** `name in reconciledFunctions` reads the prototype chain, so a handler named `constructor` or `toString` counts as a bundle function for the shared rule. Use an own-property test.
- **N4, nit:** the count rule cannot see a twin on a partially flattened artifact (the top level claims the name, so the body's copy is dropped before the count). `artifact-collections.ts` rules that shape out, but pins (f) and CONTROL are hand-written in it; the #32355 job rule shares the limit.
- **N5, nit:** pin (a) asserts the resolver call the script-node bridge makes, not a flow run, though the card's pin and the test title say "a body-B flow runs B's own function".
- **N6, nit:** on a dropped body, `unregisterFunctionsByPackage` also removes functions host code registered under that body's owner (the kind pin (b) uses).

No security finding.
